newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Alcoa 1996 yr net profit A$395 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Alcoa 1996 yr net profit A$395 mln.

text.p: Alcoa of Australia Ltd reported on Thursday a net profit of A$395 million in calendar 1996, up 15 percent from A$343.5 million in 1995.
Alcoa of Australia said the net profit after abnormal items for 1996 was A$388.3 million, which compared with A$312.7 million in 1995, an increase of 24.2 percent.
It said the abnormal item in 1996 which reduced net profit by A$6.7 million relates to severance provisions as a result of the relocation of the corporate office to Perth from Melbourne.

The alumina and aluminium producer said the higher net profit was primarily attributable to improved prices and shipments of alumina and alumina chemicals, partially offset by lower metal prices and an average higher rate of exchange of the Australia dollar when compared with the U.S. dollar.
Alcoa of Australia said sales revenue for 1996 was 6.4 percent up at A$2.53 billion as a consequence of higher exports which increased to A$2.18 billion from A$2.03 billion.
Alcoa said its tax expense rose to A$206 million in 1996 from A$188.7 million in 1995 while capital expenditure fell to A$179.9 million from A$193.5 million.
It said it paid shareholders fully franked dividends of A$380 million and a special dividend of A$100 million during 1996. The group paid dividends of A$340 million in 1995.
Alcoa of Australia is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 39.25 percent by WMC Ltd.
QBE Insurance Group Ltd owns the balance.
Alcoa commented that the 1996 profit was a satisfactory result in a year when metal and alumina markets were volatile. At 12.35 p.m. (0135 GMT), WMC shares were 20 cents up at A$8.15.
